mainTopic: Money instead of lashes: the sister case between עולא and רבי יוחנן, whether עדים זוממין need a warning, and the source that one who injures pays rather than being lashed.
overview: This amud finishes the argument between עולא and רבי יוחנן about a man who violates his sister: does he pay the קנס or get מלקות? First the גמרא shows that a lashes verse is not 'cancelled' as long as some case is left for it. Examples are עדים זוממין in a בן גרושה case, a blow worth less than a פרוטה, and a sister who is a בוגרת. רבי יוחנן's real reason is that he needs 'תחת אשר עינה' for אביי's teaching about בושת and פגם. עולא learns that teaching from רבא's reading of 'השוכב עמה' instead. Next, רבי אליעזר says עדים זוממין pay rather than get lashes because they cannot be warned, and רבא shows there is no workable moment to warn them. אביי and רב אחא challenge that proof. Then אביי argues that עדים זוממין need no warning at all, because of 'כאשר זמם'. The verse 'משפט אחד' extends this even to the בן גרושה case. Finally, רב שישא proves from the verse of men fighting near a pregnant woman that חובל בחבירו pays money and is not lashed. רב אשי challenges two assumptions behind that proof.

steps.title: The same complaint would cancel the verse about hitting a person
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא argues that if 'paying instead of lashes cancels a lashes verse' were a real problem, it would also apply to one who injures his fellow.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then one who injures his fellow as well: if so, you have cancelled 'He shall not add, lest he add'!
steps.whatsHappening: The previous daf argued that עולא's view leaves the lashes for the sister with no use. The גמרא answers by showing the same argument would hit חובל בחבירו, where everyone agrees the injurer pays.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The source for lashes for hitting another person is 'לא יוסיף פן יוסיף'. Since a חובל pays money and is not lashed, that verse should also be 'cancelled'. So the argument proves too much, unless there are cases where the verse still applies.

keyTerms.meaning: One who injures another person
You have cancelled / made it useless
He shall not add (more lashes)
If so

phrases.english: One who injures his fellow as well:
if so, you have cancelled
"He shall not add, lest he add"!

steps.triggerLanguage: חוֹבֵל בַּחֲבֵירוֹ נָמֵי, אִם כֵּן בִּטַּלְתָּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the previous daf's argument about whether עולא's view leaves the lashes for the sister with no use.
steps.kashyaTarget: The argument that a lashes verse would become useless if the sinner pays instead.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same reasoning would cancel 'לא יוסיף' in the case of חובל בחבירו, yet there the law clearly is payment.

steps.title: The same complaint would cancel the lashes for false witnesses
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא adds a second example: עדים זוממין pay money, so the lashes verse used for them would also be cancelled.
steps.simpleTranslation: False witnesses as well: if so, you have cancelled 'And it shall be, if the wicked man deserves lashes'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another case where the same complaint would apply. That case is עדים זוממין, who pay money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse 'והיה אם בן הכות הרשע' is used as the source for lashes for עדים זוממין. If they pay money, that verse seems to have no use. This strengthens the point that the complaint cannot be right as stated.

keyTerms.meaning: Witnesses proven false: other witnesses show they were somewhere else at the time
Deserving of lashes
The wicked one

phrases.english: False witnesses as well:
if so, you have cancelled
"And it shall be, if the wicked man deserves to be lashed"!

steps.triggerLanguage: עֵדִים זוֹמְמִין נָמֵי, אִם כֵּן בִּטַּלְתָּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second parallel case to step 1.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: עדים זוממין pay money, so their lashes verse would also seem to have no use.

steps.title: Both verses still apply in special cases
steps.stepSummary: Each lashes verse still applies in a case where no money is paid: the witnesses in a בן גרושה case, and the injurer whose blow caused less than a פרוטה of damage.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: for false witnesses, the verse can be fulfilled in the case of a בן גרושה or בן חלוצה. For one who injures his fellow, it can be fulfilled where he struck him with a blow that does not cause a פרוטה's worth of damage.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that these lashes verses are not really cancelled. Each one still has cases where money is not paid, so lashes are given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some false testimony can't be 'done back' to the witnesses or paid for, such as falsely calling a כהן a בן גרושה. Then the witnesses are lashed. A blow worth less than a פרוטה brings no payment, so the hitter is lashed. So a verse is not 'cancelled' as long as some case is left for it.

keyTerms.meaning: It is possible to fulfill it (to find a use for the verse)
Son of a divorcée, who is unfit to serve as a כהן
Son of a woman released through חליצה, who is also unfit as a כהן
Worth a פרוטה, the smallest amount that counts as money

steps.whatToRemember: A verse is not 'cancelled' if at least one case remains where it applies.

phrases.english: Rather: false witnesses,
it is possible to fulfill it
with a son of a divorcée or a son of a חלוצה.
One who injures his fellow as well,
there is a way to fulfill it:
for example, where he struck him a blow
that does not contain a פרוטה's worth.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: עֵדִים זוֹמְמִין, אֶפְשָׁר לְקַיּוֹמַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the problems of steps 1 and 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Finding leftover cases where the lashes verse still applies
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Paying money would leave the lashes verse with no use at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: The verses still apply where no payment is possible (the בן גרושה case, or damage under a פרוטה).

steps.title: The sister case can also be fulfilled
steps.stepSummary: Following the same logic, the lashes for the sister still apply when she is a בוגרת, who gets no fine. So רבי יוחנן's complaint against עולא falls away.
steps.simpleTranslation: His sister as well: it can be fulfilled with his sister who is a בוגרת!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses the answer it just gave against רבי יוחנן. Under עולא's view, the sister's lashes are not cancelled either.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קנס is paid only for a נערה. If the sister is a בוגרת, there is no fine, so lashes apply. So the 'cancelled verse' argument cannot be רבי יוחנן's real reason for rejecting עולא.

keyTerms.meaning: His sister
A grown woman, past the age of נערה, who receives no קנס
There is a way to fulfill it

phrases.english: His sister as well:
there is a way to fulfill it
with his sister who is a grown woman!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲחוֹתוֹ נָמֵי, אִיכָּא לְקַיּוֹמַהּ בַּאֲחוֹתוֹ בּוֹגֶרֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies step 3's answer to the sister case, which weakens רבי יוחנן's argument.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's reason for rejecting עולא's view.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under עולא, the lashes for the sister still apply to a בוגרת, so no verse is cancelled.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן needs the verse for אביי's teaching
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן rejects עולא's גזירה שוה for a different reason. He needs the words 'תחת אשר עינה' to teach that בושת and פגם are paid on top of the fine.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן could say to you: this verse 'because he afflicted her' is needed for אביי's teaching. As אביי said, the verse says 'because he afflicted her'. From this we learn that there is also payment for humiliation and degradation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives רבי יוחנן a new reason. The words 'תחת' that עולא uses for his גזירה שוה are already being used for something else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי reads 'תחת אשר עינה' to mean the fifty is only for the pain of the act. So בושת and פגם must be paid in addition. Since this verse is busy teaching that, רבי יוחנן won't use it for a גזירה שוה.

keyTerms.meaning: He needs it (for a different teaching)
Because he afflicted her
By inference, from this we learn
Payment for humiliation
Payment for degradation (her lowered value)

phrases.english: רבי יוחנן could say to you:
this verse "because he afflicted her"
he needs it for that which אביי taught.
As אביי said: the verse says:
"Because he afflicted her".
This "because he afflicted her":
by inference, there is also humiliation and degradation.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָךְ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 4 knocked out the old reason, this gives רבי יוחנן a new one.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The verse is needed for a different teaching
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוחנן rejects עולא because the sister's lashes would be cancelled.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יוחנן rejects the גזירה שוה because 'תחת אשר עינה' is used for אביי's teaching about בושת and פגם.

steps.title: Where does עולא learn אביי's teaching?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how עולא, who uses the verse for his גזירה שוה, knows that בושת and פגם are paid.
steps.simpleTranslation: And עולא?
steps.whatsHappening: This short question sets up the next step. If עולא uses 'תחת' for his גזירה שוה, where does he get the rule about בושת and פגם?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone agrees that בושת and פגם are paid. So עולא must have a different source for that rule, and the גמרא wants to know what it is.

keyTerms.meaning: And עולא (how does he deal with this?)

phrases.english: And עולא?
phrases.notes: The גמרא is asking: since עולא uses this פסוק for his comparison, where does he learn about humiliation and degradation?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעוּלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns step 5's point around and asks it of עולא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: עולא's source for paying בושת and פגם.

steps.title: עולא learns it from רבא's reading
steps.stepSummary: עולא learns about בושת and פגם from the words 'השוכב עמה': the fifty is for the pleasure of lying with her, so the other payments are separate.
steps.simpleTranslation: He learns it from רבא. As רבא said, the verse says: 'And the man who lay with her shall give the girl's father fifty silver'. The fifty is for the pleasure of lying with her, so by inference there is also payment for humiliation and degradation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that עולא uses a different phrase in the same verse to learn the same rule. That leaves 'תחת' free for his גזירה שוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא reads 'השוכב עמה' as saying what the fifty pays for: the pleasure of the act. That means בושת and פגם are extra. So both sides agree on the rule but learn it from different words.

keyTerms.meaning: He derives it from
The one who lay with her
The pleasure of lying (with her)
Fifty (שקלים of) silver, the קנס

steps.whatToRemember: עולא and רבי יוחנן agree that בושת and פגם are paid. They argue only over which words of the verse teach it, and so whether 'תחת' is free for a גזירה שוה.

phrases.english: He derives it from רבא.
As רבא said: the verse says:
"And the man who lay with her shall give
to the father of the girl fifty silver":
for the pleasure of lying with her, fifty;
by inference, there is also humiliation and degradation.

steps.triggerLanguage: נָפְקָא לֵיהּ מִדְּרָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: עולא learns בושת and פגם from 'השוכב עמה', as רבא taught, so 'תחת' stays free for his גזירה שוה.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: false witnesses can't be warned
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר says עדים זוממין pay money and are not lashed because they cannot be given a proper התראה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: false witnesses pay money and are not lashed, because they are not people who can be warned.
steps.whatsHappening: A new opinion is brought. It gives a different reason why עדים זוממין pay instead of getting lashes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Lashes need התראה, a warning given before the sin. If a proper warning is impossible for these witnesses, lashes cannot be given, and money is the only punishment left.

keyTerms.meaning: They pay money
They do not receive lashes
People who can be given a warning

phrases.english: רבי אליעזר says:
false witnesses pay money
and are not lashed,
because they are not people who can be warned.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new reason for why עדים זוממין pay instead of being lashed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: עדים זוממין pay and are not lashed, because they cannot be properly warned.

steps.title: רבא proves there is no good time to warn them
steps.stepSummary: רבא shows that every possible moment to warn false witnesses fails: before, during, or after their testimony.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Know that this is so. When would we warn them? If we warn them at the start, they will say 'We forgot.' If we warn them at the moment of testifying, they will back off and not testify. If we warn them at the end, what was, was.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא supports רבי אליעזר. He goes through each possible time to warn the witnesses and shows that none of them works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An early warning can be brushed off with 'we forgot'. A warning just before they testify would make them back off and not testify at all. A warning afterward is useless because the testimony is already given. So עדים זוממין truly cannot be warned.

keyTerms.meaning: Know (that this is true), a proof
Let us warn them
We forgot
They will withdraw
What happened, happened

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי אליעזר, עדים זוממין pay rather than get lashes because no workable התראה is possible for them.

phrases.english: רבא said: Know that it is so.
When would we warn them?
Let us warn them at the start,
they will say: We forgot.
Let us warn them at the moment of the act,
they will back off and not testify.
Let us warn them at the end,
what was, was.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: תִּדַּע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי אליעזר's statement in step 8.
steps.raayaObject: רבי אליעזר's claim that עדים זוממין cannot be warned.
steps.raayaSupportSource: Logical proof: going through each possible time for a warning (before, during, after) and showing each one fails.

steps.title: אביי: warn them right after they speak
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges רבא: we could warn the witnesses in the short moment right after they testify.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי objects: Why not warn them within the short time right after they finish speaking?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks רבא's proof that there is no possible moment to warn עדים זוממין. He suggests one more moment that might work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא said a warning after the testimony is too late, because the testimony is already done. אביי answers that for a few seconds after speaking (תוך כדי דיבור), witnesses can still take back their words, so the testimony is not locked in yet. A warning given then would be on time.

keyTerms.meaning: Strongly objects to it
The few seconds right after speaking, when a person can still take back his words
A warning given before a sin, needed for court punishment

phrases.english: Abaye objects to this:
But let us warn them within the time of speaking?
phrases.notes: These are the few seconds after they finish, while they could still take back their testimony.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ אַבָּיֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the 'after the testimony' part of רבא's proof
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that a warning after the testimony is useless
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Right after speaking, the testimony can still be taken back, so a warning then is still on time.

steps.title: רב אחא: warn first, then hint during testimony
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרב איקא suggests warning the witnesses before they testify and reminding them with hints while they speak.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא son of רב איקא objects: Why not warn them at the start, and then hint to them while they testify?
steps.whatsHappening: A second challenge to רבא. רב אחא offers a way around the problem of warning too early.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא said a warning before the testimony fails because the witnesses can claim they forgot it. רב אחא answers that we could warn them first and then signal to them during the testimony to remind them, so they cannot say they forgot.

keyTerms.meaning: From the start, beforehand
Hints, signals

phrases.aramaic: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִיקָא:
phrases.english: Rav Acha son of Rav Ika objects to this:
But let us warn them from the start
and hint to them with hints?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִיקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second attack on רבא's proof, this time on the 'before the testimony' part
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that a warning before the testimony fails because they may forget
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Hints during the testimony remind them of the earlier warning, so they cannot claim they forgot.

steps.title: אביי: false witnesses need no warning at all
steps.stepSummary: אביי gives a new reason: עדים זוממין do not need a warning, because they are punished exactly as they plotted, and they plotted to kill without a real warning.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי then said: What I said is not a real point. If you think עדים זוממין need a warning, then when we don't warn them, we won't kill them. But is there such a thing, where they tried to kill someone without a warning, and they themselves need a warning? We need 'and you shall do to him as he plotted to do to his brother,' and that would be missing.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי sets aside the whole argument about when we could warn them. He says the question does not even start, because false witnesses never need a warning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah says to do to false witnesses 'as they plotted' (כאשר זמם). They tried to get an innocent man killed without a true warning. If they needed a warning to be punished, their punishment would no longer match what they plotted. So no warning is needed, and the reason they pay money and are not lashed must come from somewhere else.

keyTerms.meaning: Then he said (changing his earlier view)
If it enters your mind, if you think
As he plotted, the Torah's rule for punishing false witnesses

steps.whatToRemember: According to אביי, עדים זוממין never need a warning, because their punishment must mirror what they plotted.

phrases.english: Abaye then said:
What I said is not a real point.
If it enters your mind
that false witnesses need a warning,
then when we do not warn them
we do not kill them.
Is there such a thing
where they tried to kill without a warning,
and they themselves need a warning?
But we require
"And you shall do to him as he plotted to do to his brother,"
and that would be missing.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲדַר אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: לָאו מִילְּתָא הִיא דַּאֲמַרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the debate about the timing of a warning with a new principle that no warning is needed
steps.terutzResolutionType: Removes the premise of the question
steps.terutzHavaAmina: עדים זוממין need a warning, so we must find a moment when warning them could work.
steps.terutzMaskana: They need no warning, because their punishment must match the warning-free death they plotted.

steps.title: רב סמא: what about the son of a divorcee?
steps.stepSummary: רב סמא challenges אביי: in cases like בן גרושה, the punishment does not come from 'as he plotted', so there a warning should be needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב סמא son of רב ירמיה objects: But if so, in the case of a son of a divorcee or a son of a חלוצה, which is not included in 'as he plotted,' a warning should be needed!
steps.whatsHappening: רב סמא tests אביי's reason with a case where 'as he plotted' cannot apply.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If witnesses falsely say a כהן is a בן גרושה or בן חלוצה, we cannot make the witnesses into such a person. Their punishment is lashes, not 'as he plotted.' So אביי's reason does not cover this case, and these witnesses should need a warning.

keyTerms.meaning: But now, according to your reasoning
Son of a divorcee, a כהן who is disqualified from כהונה
Son of a woman who had חליצה, also disqualified from כהונה

phrases.aramaic: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב סַמָּא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יִרְמְיָה:
phrases.english: Rav Samma son of Rav Yirmeya objects to this:
But if so,
the son of a divorcee and the son of a chalutza,
which are not included from "as he plotted" —
let them need a warning!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב סַמָּא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יִרְמְיָה: אֶלָּא מֵעַתָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges אביי's new reason
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's reason that no warning is needed because of 'as he plotted'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In בן גרושה cases 'as he plotted' does not apply, so the reason fails and a warning should be needed there.

steps.title: One law for all false witnesses
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers from the verse 'one law shall be for you': all false witnesses follow the same rule, so none need a warning.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'One law shall be for you,' meaning a law that is equal for all of you.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends אביי by showing that the special cases follow the main rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since ordinary עדים זוממין need no warning, the verse 'one law' tells us that all false witnesses are treated the same. So even in the case of בן גרושה, where 'as he plotted' does not apply, no warning is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: The verse says
One law, the same rule for everyone

steps.whatToRemember: All עדים זוממין, even in unusual cases like בן גרושה, need no warning, because of 'one law for all of you.'

phrases.english: The verse says:
"One law shall be for you,"
a law that is equal for all of you.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר קְרָא: מִשְׁפַּט אֶחָד יִהְיֶה לָכֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב סמא's challenge
steps.terutzResolutionType: Verse that extends the main rule to the special case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Cases outside 'as he plotted' should need a warning.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'One law' makes all false witnesses equal, so none need a warning.

steps.title: רב שישא: a new source for one who injures
steps.stepSummary: רב שישא בריה דרב אידי brings a source that חובל בחבירו pays money and is not lashed, from the verse about men fighting who hit a pregnant woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שישא son of רב אידי said: One who injures his fellow also pays money and is not lashed. We learn it from here: 'And if men fight and hit a pregnant woman and her children come out.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new point. רב שישא gives a source for the rule that someone who injures another pays money and does not get lashes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the verse, a man hits a pregnant woman, and the Torah makes him pay money for her lost child. רב שישא learns from here that one who injures pays money instead of being lashed. The next step explains why this verse proves it.

keyTerms.meaning: One who injures his fellow
He pays money
He is not lashed

phrases.aramaic: רַב שִׁישָׁא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי אָמַר:
phrases.english: Rav Sheisha son of Rav Idi said:
One who injures his fellow also,
pays money and is not lashed,
from here:
"And if men fight
and hit a pregnant woman and her children come out."

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב שִׁישָׁא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new point about the source for the injurer paying money
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who injures his fellow pays money and is not lashed, learned from the verse of men fighting who hit a pregnant woman.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: the fight was a deadly one
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר explains that the verse is about a fight where the men were trying to kill, as shown by 'a life for a life.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אלעזר said: The verse is talking about a fight that involves death, as it is written: 'And if there is harm, you shall give a life for a life.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings רבי אלעזר's reading to show why the verse works as a source for רב שישא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The next verse speaks of 'a life for a life,' so רבי אלעזר says the men were fighting to kill each other. Even in such a serious fight, the Torah sets money as the payment for hurting the woman. This supports רב שישא: injuring leads to paying money, not lashes.

keyTerms.meaning: A fight that involves death, where they tried to kill each other
A life for a life

phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar said:
The verse is talking about a fight that involves death,
as it is written:
"And if there is harm,
you shall give a life for a life."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: בְּמַצּוּת שֶׁבְּמִיתָה הַכָּתוּב מְדַבֵּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב שישא's source by explaining what kind of fight the verse describes
steps.raayaObject: רב שישא's claim that the verse of the pregnant woman teaches that an injurer pays money
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי אלעזר's reading, based on 'a life for a life,' that the verse is about a deadly fight

steps.title: What exactly was the case of the fighting men?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the case of the fighting men must have looked. If they had not been warned, they could not be killed.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? If they did not warn him, why would he be killed?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next move of רב שישא's proof by asking what the case of the fighting men must have been. It points out that without a warning, nobody can get the death penalty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'a life for a life', so the fighter can be killed. In בית דין, a death penalty needs a proper warning (התראה). So the case must involve a warning, and the next step builds on that.

keyTerms.meaning: What are the circumstances? What does the case look like?
They warned him (gave him a formal warning before the act)
He is killed (gets the death penalty)

phrases.english: What are the circumstances?
If they did not warn him,
phrases.notes: Here 'him' is the fighter who was trying to kill the other man.

phrases.english: why is he killed?
phrases.notes: This refers to 'a life for a life' from the previous step. Without a warning, בית דין cannot put anyone to death.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכִי דָמֵי? אִי דְּלָא אַתְרוֹ בֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on רבי אלעזר's point that the fighters were trying to kill. Since they can be killed, it asks what the case must have been.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the fighters in the פסוק were warned, given that they can receive the death penalty.

steps.title: They were warned, and the warning also covers injury, yet the פסוק says he only pays
steps.stepSummary: The fighter must have been warned about killing. A warning for the severe act also counts for the lighter act of injuring, yet the תורה says he pays money. So חובל בחבירו pays and is not lashed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is obvious that they warned him. A person warned about a severe matter counts as warned about a lighter matter. And yet the Merciful One said: 'And no harm happens, he shall surely be punished' (with money).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the fighter must have been warned about killing. That warning also counts as a warning about injuring, and still the תורה gives only a money payment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Lashes for injuring someone would need a warning. Here the fighter was warned, because the warning about killing covers the lighter act of injuring too. Even so, when no one dies, the פסוק says only 'he shall be punished', meaning he pays money. This shows that חובל בחבירו pays and is not lashed.

keyTerms.meaning: Someone warned about a severe matter (here, killing)
Someone warned about a lighter matter (here, injuring)
The Merciful One (a name for ה׳ as the Giver of the תורה)
He shall surely be punished (understood as paying money)

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the heart of רב שישא's proof. It depends on the rule that a warning for the severe act also covers the lighter act, and רב אשי attacks exactly that point next.

phrases.english: Rather, it is obvious that they warned him,
and one who is warned about a severe matter,
phrases.notes: The severe matter is killing the other man.

phrases.english: is considered warned about a lighter matter.
phrases.notes: The lighter matter is injuring, which on its own would normally get lashes.

phrases.english: And yet the Merciful One said:
'And no harm happens, he shall surely be punished.'
phrases.notes: שמות 21:22. 'Punished' here means paying money, not lashes.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא פְּשִׁיטָא דְּאַתְרוֹ בֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 17 and finishes רב שישא's proof.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The fighter was warned about killing, and that warning also counts for injuring. Still the פסוק gives only money, so money replaces lashes.
steps.raayaObject: חובל בחבירו pays money and is not lashed.
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמות 21:22, 'ולא יהיה אסון ענוש יענש', read together with the rule that a warning for the severe act covers the lighter one.

steps.title: Who says a warning for the severe act covers the lighter act?
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי challenges the proof. Maybe a warning about killing does not count as a warning about injuring.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי objected: From where do we know that one warned about a severe matter counts as warned about a lighter matter? Maybe he does not!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי attacks the foundation of the proof. He questions the rule that a warning about killing also counts as a warning about injuring.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof needs the fighter to have been properly warned about injuring. Only then is it surprising that he pays instead of being lashed. If the warning for killing does not cover injuring, he simply was never warned for lashes, and the פסוק proves nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: Strongly objects to it
From where (do we know)?
Perhaps

phrases.english: Rav Ashi strongly objected to it:
From where do we know that one warned about a severe matter
is considered warned about a lighter matter?
Perhaps he is not!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ, רַב אָשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the key assumption that made the proof in step 18 work.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule 'מותרה לדבר חמור הוי מותרה לדבר הקל' used in רב שישא's proof.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a warning for killing does not cover injuring, the fighter was never warned for lashes. Then his paying money proves nothing about חובל בחבירו in general.

steps.title: Who says death is more severe than lashes?
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי adds a second challenge. Even if a warning for the severe act covers the lighter one, how do we know death is the severe one compared to lashes?
steps.simpleTranslation: Even if you say he is considered warned, from where do we know that death is more severe?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives a second, backup challenge. Even if we accept the rule about warnings, he asks how we know death is more severe than lashes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule only works if the warning was for the more severe punishment. If lashes might count as more severe than death, then a warning for death would not cover lashes. The proof would fall apart again.

keyTerms.meaning: If you will say (even if you accept this point)
Death is more severe

steps.confusionAlert: It seems obvious that death is worse than lashes, but רב אשי is asking for a real source, not a feeling. Do not assume the question is silly.

phrases.english: If you will say that he is considered warned,
from where do we know that death is more severe?
phrases.notes: He means more severe than lashes, the punishment for injuring.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם תִּמְצָא לוֹמַר הָוֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second layer of רב אשי's objection. It grants the first point for argument's sake and attacks another assumption.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that the death penalty is the 'severe matter' compared to lashes.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If lashes might count as more severe than death, then a warning for death would not cover lashes. The proof that money replaces lashes would fail.
